items.name: Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (Zeitz MOCAA)
items.note: Africa's largest museum of contemporary art from the continent and its diaspora, in converted grain silos at the V&A Waterfront.

items.name: Museum of Black Civilisations (Musée des Civilisations Noires)
items.note: Opened 2018 as a pan-African museum and a focal point in the debate over restitution of looted African heritage.

items.name: Grand Egyptian Museum
items.note: One of the largest archaeological museums in the world, holding the complete Tutankhamun collection beside the Giza plateau.

items.name: Museum of African Contemporary Art Al Maaden (MACAAL)
items.note: One of Africa's few independent, privately funded contemporary art museums, focused on artists working across the continent.

items.name: Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art
items.note: Holds the most comprehensive collection of modern and contemporary Arab art, spanning the 1840s to the present.

items.name: Museum of Islamic Art
items.note: I. M. Pei's purpose-built museum on the Corniche, holding one of the world's foremost collections of Islamic art.

items.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
items.note: Jean Nouvel-designed universal museum on Saadiyat Island that hangs world art chronologically rather than by region.

items.name: Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art
items.note: Holds an extraordinary, rarely shown collection of Western modernism alongside major Iranian modern art.

items.name: Istanbul Modern
items.note: Türkiye's first modern and contemporary art museum, reopened in 2023 in a Renzo Piano building on the Karaköy waterfront.

items.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya (CSMVS)
items.note: India's leading encyclopaedic museum, covering art and archaeology from prehistory to the modern period.

items.name: Museum of Art & Photography (MAP)
items.note: Privately founded museum with a deep South Asian photography and popular-culture collection and an unusually open digital archive.

items.name: National Gallery Singapore
items.note: Holds the world's largest public collection of modern Southeast Asian art, in the former Supreme Court and City Hall.

items.name: Museum MACAN
items.note: Indonesia's first museum with a modern and contemporary collection of both Indonesian and international art.

items.name: M+
items.note: Asia's flagship museum of twentieth- and twenty-first-century visual culture, spanning art, design, architecture and moving image.

items.name: Power Station of Art
items.note: Mainland China's first state-run contemporary art museum, in a converted riverside power plant; hosts the Shanghai Biennale.

items.name: Mori Art Museum
items.note: Contemporary art museum on the 53rd floor of Roppongi Hills, known for ambitious pan-Asian survey exhibitions.

items.name: Benesse House Museum
items.note: Tadao Ando museum-and-hotel that anchors Benesse Art Site Naoshima, the model for site-specific island art tourism.

items.name: National Museum of Korea
items.note: Korea's flagship national museum and one of the most-visited museums in the world.

items.name: Museum of Old and New Art (Mona)
items.note: Privately funded subterranean museum on the Berriedale peninsula that reshaped Tasmania's cultural economy.

items.name: Art Gallery of New South Wales
items.note: New South Wales' state gallery, with major Australian, Asian and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander collections.

items.name: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki
items.note: New Zealand's largest art institution, with the country's most significant holdings of Māori and Pacific portraiture and contemporary art.

items.name: São Paulo Museum of Art (MASP)
items.note: Latin America's most important art collection, in Lina Bo Bardi's landmark elevated building on Avenida Paulista.

items.name: Instituto Inhotim
items.note: Vast open-air museum and botanical garden with permanent pavilions built for individual artists' large-scale installations.

items.name: Museo de Arte Latinoamericano de Buenos Aires (MALBA)
items.note: The key reference collection for twentieth-century Latin American art, from Frida Kahlo to Argentine conceptualism.

items.name: Museo Jumex
items.note: David Chipperfield-designed home of Latin America's largest private contemporary art collection.

items.name: Museo de Arte de Lima (MALI)
items.note: Peru's principal art museum, covering three thousand years from pre-Columbian work to contemporary Peruvian art.

items.name: Garage Museum of Contemporary Art
items.note: Russia's leading contemporary art institution, in a Rem Koolhaas conversion of a Soviet pavilion in Gorky Park.

items.name: Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw (Muzeum Sztuki Nowoczesnej)
items.note: Opened its purpose-built Thomas Phifer home on Plac Defilad in 2024, Poland's main platform for contemporary art.

items.name: Tate Modern
items.note: The UK's national museum of international modern and contemporary art, in the former Bankside Power Station.

items.name: Centre Pompidou
items.note: Home of the Musée National d'Art Moderne, Europe's largest modern and contemporary art collection.

items.name: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA)
items.note: The institution that largely defined the canon of twentieth-century modern art, from painting to film and design.

items.name: National Museum of African American History and Culture
items.note: The only national museum devoted exclusively to African American history, art and culture, on the National Mall.
